sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and float rule wording
sections.what: Holds the rule code and the message telling developers to use exact integer fractions.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the rule text together for consistent messages. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: _contains_float
sections.title: Float type detector
sections.what: Checks whether a type label contains a float type, including the Float name used by table libraries.
sections.why: Likely reason: one helper keeps the float test the same for every place the rule checks. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: It checks the whole annotation tree, so a float buried inside a larger type still counts.

sections.name: check_source
sections.title: Share float checker
sections.what: Scans a Python file for share values declared with a float type in variables, function arguments, or table columns, and returns a violation for each.
sections.why: Likely reason: catches approximate share values where they are declared. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Only names containing share are checked, so a float stored under another name would not be flagged.

summary: Flags land share values stored as decimal floating-point numbers, which can round incorrectly, and asks for exact fractions instead.
purpose: Protects the accuracy of land shares by forbidding approximate numbers.
why: The message says to use exact integer fractions. The reason is stated in the message text: floats are inexact.
how: Parses a Python file and checks three places: annotated variables with share in the name, function arguments with share in the name, and table column definitions with share in the name that use a float type. Each match is recorded as a violation.
inputs: Python source text and the file path it came from.
outputs: A list of violation reports pointing to the rule and the message about exact fractions.
risks: Source that is not valid Python raises an error. Only direct calls named Column are checked, so other table helpers would be missed.
debug: If a share is flagged wrongly, check the name contains share and the annotation. If a float slips through, check whether it is written in a form this check does not look at.
